correctness.rationale: For the fixed simple cubic graph n>=7, cut-edge counts squeeze |outside|<=e<=|inside|; both monochromatic rings attain n, and equality is precisely one opposite neighbor at every vertex. Eliminating the inner signs gives the Laurent operator whose cleared polynomial is (E-1)(E^5-1)(E^2+1). The cyclic shift is diagonalizable, so the outer word is a sum of four- and five-periodic words. On the Z/4 x Z/5 grid, distinct rows differ by a nonzero fixed number; with entries ±1 the difference is ±2, forcing both rows constant and the five-periodic term constant. Thus no mixed word survives. The inner sign formula forbids singleton outer runs; it leaves only ++-- with zero alternating Fourier coefficient in period four, and ++--- and its complement in period five, besides constants. All these solve the recurrence and give actual signs. Their fundamental periods and the unique inner word yield the claimed labelled counts even at multiples of 20. Inspected the supplied script and notes without execution; the reported finite census and graph checks are corroboration, not the all-n proof.
